purpose: Make adopter README and human-facing product documentation about the target repository — audience, problem, features, and provenance for the product's own claims — welcoming before technical details become necessary.

required_sections.heading: Why this exists
required_sections.question: What human situation and consequence make this project matter?

required_sections.heading: What this project is
required_sections.question: Who is it for, what does it do, and what does it not claim?

required_sections.heading: What you can make or use
required_sections.question: What useful output, workflow, or decision can the reader reach?

required_sections.heading: How it works
required_sections.question: Can the mechanism be understood before the architecture?

required_sections.heading: Evidence and boundaries
required_sections.question: Which product claims are supported and where does the project stop?

required_sections.heading: Try it
required_sections.question: Is there a smallest useful next action?

adopter_readme_policy.scope: Applies to README.md (and equivalent product-entry pages) in target/adopter repositories. Does not restrict this helper repository's own README, which documents CGM.
must_be_about: problem and consequence the product addresses
what the product is and is not
features, outputs, or workflows the reader can use
how the product works at reader altitude
provenance and citations only for the target product's own claims
must_not: cite, promote, justify, or defend Content Generation Modules (CGM) or content-generation-modules
narrate how images were generated (provider, prompt pipeline, seed, model, ChatGPT workflow)
narrate writing-style methodology (writing-direction, hsw, scan-first recipe, bold heuristics) as README story
link IMAGE_GUIDE, prompt records, or helper templates as if they were product features
treat image regeneration instructions as README content
adopter_readme_policy.image_provenance: Record role, prompt, exact text, dimensions, alt intent, crop, rejection, and review in .content-system/asset-manifest.json (or linked prompt records under the adapter). Place images in the README with useful alt text beside the product idea they explain; do not turn the README into an image-pipeline guide.
adopter_readme_policy.citations: Cite only sources that support the target product's claims. Helper research, brand, and image guides stay in the pinned CGM checkout for agents — not in adopter README prose.
adopter_readme_policy.optional_product_lineage: A short prior-work note is allowed only when it explains the target product's own lineage or related products. Do not paste CGM prior-work catalogs or helper migration guides.

scanability_policy.heading_rule: Use descriptive headings that tell the reader what they will learn or gain.
scanability_policy.bolding_rule: Use one short meaningful anchor when helpful, usually 2–8 words, for a problem, outcome, mechanism, proof, or boundary.
scanability_policy.scan_test: Read only headings, bold phrases, and link text; they should communicate the problem, promise, mechanism, boundary, and next action.
scanability_policy.accessibility_rule: Keep the text understandable when bold styling disappears and use semantic headings for structure.

story_policy.worked_example: Include at least one concrete example grounded in the target repository; label hypothetical examples clearly.
story_policy.reader_paths: Explain for the primary human reader first; add a distinct developer or researcher path when it helps them act or reproduce the work.

evidence_policy.supports_rule: Say what the cited source establishes in plain language about the target product.
evidence_policy.limits_rule: Say what the same source leaves unproven; do not claim more than its evidence supports.
evidence_policy.citation_rule: Link important public product claims directly to immutable repository evidence or a direct external source near the claim. Do not cite CGM to justify the product story.
evidence_policy.truth_boundary: A valid citation establishes traceability, not truth; preserve source quality limits and human review.

visual_policy.use_when: the target repository has a visual contract, committed narrative assets, or a request for visual direction
visual_policy.readme_vs_manifest: Helper and agents use required_guides and required_image_record_fields when creating assets. Adopter README shows the image with alt text; provenance fields live in the adapter asset manifest, not as a README 'Image generation and use' section.

review_questions: Can a first-time reader explain why the project exists after twenty seconds?
Does the first screen feel welcoming before it becomes technical?
Can the reader distinguish shipped evidence from plans and unknowns?
Can a reviewer see what the product evidence supports and what it does not establish?
Can a fresh agent reproduce the source trail from the target repository and this pinned contract?
Do the visuals clarify one human idea and remain useful when stacked on a narrow screen?
Is image provenance recorded in .content-system/asset-manifest (or linked records) rather than narrated in the README?
Does the adopter README avoid citing CGM, describing the image-gen pipeline, or teaching writing-style methodology?
